steps.text: Arrange 1/2 of strawberries in baked pastry shell. Place remaining strawberries in a medium saucepan.
Add sugar to the strawberries in the saucepan; place over medium heat and bring to a boil, stirring frequently.

Whisk cornstarch and water together in a small bowl. Gradually stir cornstarch mixture into boiling strawberry mixture. Reduce heat and simmer mixture until thickened, about 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour cooked strawberry mixture over berries in pastry shell. Refrigerate until chilled and set, at least 3 hours.
Before serving, whip cream in a medium bowl until soft peaks form.
Serve each slice of pie with a dollop of whipped cream. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Pie
raw_recipe.description: Strawberry pie is a favorite, and this five-ingredient, picture-perfect version couldn't be easier to whip up. It's a must-try after berry picking!

review.reviewBody: This stuff is the bomb! I cheated, however, and modified it a little according to others opinions. Instead of leaving half of the berries unmashed and mashing the other half, I did 3/4 unmashed and 1/4 mashed. It was PERFECT - not too sweet and jammy that way! I still kept the measurements of cornstarch at 3T, but I cut down on the sugar (used 3/4 cup) and the water (used 1/2 cup). I did NOT cook the mixture for 10 minutes like the recipe says. I added everything together in the cold pot, then turned it on to med-high and stirred it CONSTANTLY until it started boiling. Leave it at boiling for 2-3 minutes. It gets thick really fast. I let it cool for a couple of minutes and poured it on the pie. After only 1 hour in the fridge, it was set perfectly!

We loved this pie for Easter. I used more strawberries in the sauce than it called for. The clencher that took it over the top was after the shell was baked I melted about 2 oz. of semi-sweet chocolate chips in the microwave and "painted" the inside of the crust with the melted chocolate! Unbelievably awesome! Strawberry pies are notorious for getting soggy - with the painted chocolate crust that was avoided. After you paint the crust be sure to put it in the refrigerator and let the chocolate set up before you fill it.
For a great taste, use gingerale instead of water. What it does for the flavor is unbelievable.

I've made a silimar version of this pie for several years and the priamry differences are: I use fewer mashed strawberries and incorporated them into the simple syrup I made. For the simple syrup I used 1 cup water, 2 tablespoons corn starch and I cup sugar. Cook this mixture over meduim heat until thick and clear. Remove from heat and add 2 tablespoons strawberry Jell-O powder. Add mashed strawberries and proceed as directed. This give flavor and color to the pie.

I have made this pie several times for special get togethers. It’s requested now. I paint my crust with chocolate (3 tblsp. butter, 1/2 cup chocolate chips melted in double boiler. Cool to touch. Pour in pie shell and paint up the sides. Place in fridge until chocolate hardens. This keeps the crust from getting soggy.) I also cut the strawberries in the pie shell in half, just because.

I was able to use frozen strawberries for the mashed part! And only one pot, no bowl. Turned out fabulous. We were overrun with strawberries in the summer, so I mashed 2 cups and put it in a bag in the freezer. Now, in the middle of winter, I only have to pay for one pint of strawberries to cut up. I defrosted the mashed strawberries by putting the bag in cool water, then dumped it in a medium pot with the mixed cornstarch/water/sugar. Oh, I only used 1/2c water and 3/4c sugar because watery and overwhelming otherwise. Boiled until thick. Let cool in pot for 10-15 min while cut up the new strawberries. Stirred cut strawberries into pot, poured into crust and done. One pot. Simple. So tasty!

We both liked this recipe for strawberry pie. I had fresh strawberries that were still in season and thought that they were sweet enough, so I cut the sugar to 1/2 cup. I only used 1/2 cup water with the 3T cornstarch since so many said that theirs had turned out soupy. Mine didn't. I put the strawberries in the pan with the sugar and once the sugar was melted, I poured in the cornstarch and water mixture. Left that come to a boil and kept stirring. Once it felt really thick I poured it over the strawberries in the pie shell. Set it in the refrigerator uncovered for about half an hour to cool it and then covered it with saran wrap. I would make this again!

I love this recipe. I changed the pie crust to Graham cracker crust and I add one tablespoon of lemon juice. I also pureed the strawberries that I cooked. I let it cooked for 3 hours and refrigerated over night. It came out great. I have made 3 pies and have away 2 of the pies. Everyone loves them

This pie did not set. I read through the instructions several times and no where did it say to cool the filling before pouring it over the fruit which causes the thr berries to cook and release liquid, hence making the pie runny. What a waste of good strawberries and time.

I am from NJ and just picked strawberries from a local farm, so this recipe caught my eye. I made it twice this week because the family loved it! It was pretty for the Fourth of July. First I made it with the freshly picked strawberries, and the second time I made a combination of store-bought strawberries and blueberries. Change: lessen the sugar to 1/3 cup as suggested by other users. I used a pre-made pastry shell and added flavor by crumbling animal crackers and sugar cookies into a fine powder and adding a sprinkle of cinnamon. Before baking it I caked the powder mixture onto both sides of the pastry shell and brushed it with a beaten egg to get the sides a pretty golden brown. I took the suggestion of another baker and let it set in the refridgerator 12-24 hours before serving. I also made a homemade whipped cream. This recipe is definitely a keeper!

Usually I am irritated by folks that alter recipes but here I am doing just that. 
My husband loves strawberries but with just 2 of us at home, I thought tarts would be better. I read the other reviews and decreased the sugar to ¾ cup. The filling made 30 small 3” tarts so I froze them. I read that Tapioca Starch is better where freezing is required. 
THEY WERE GREAT!!
Loved this! So simple and delicious!!!!

Great recipe except for some ambiguity. The recipe calls for a "quart" of strawberries. I assume in this instance "quart" means volume and not weight, because there's no way 32 ounces of strawberries would fit into a 9 inch pie crust. But since most stores sell them by weight, it would have been less confusing for the recipe to call for a pound or 16 ounces of berries, which is in fact a pint by weight. Would've given it 5 stars, but had to take off a star due to that issue.

Ok, I searched several recipes for strawberry pie and tweaked this one. I only used 1/2 cup of water and 5 tablespoons of cornstarch. 1/4 along with sugar and a squeeze of lemon juice brought to boil stirring for 5 minutes. Made slurry with remaining 1/4 water & cornstarch added to pan stirring constantly for about 7 minutes. Thickened nicely. Let sit on stove off burner for about 10-15 minutes before adding to other strawberries & filling pie shell. Came out nice and firm and delicious.

I added 1 tbsp lemon juice to the mixture and mashed some of the strawberries with a fork (1.5 cups) Also brushed melted butter on the crust before baking it as suggested in another recipe. My first attempt at a strawberry pie and it will be on repeat.i was surprised by how easy it was to make.
I’m so pleased to find this recipe. I don’t really like pies but this is delicious. I will definitely make it again.

Delicious! I was short on time and used store bought crust, I'll be making it again with a homemade crust which will make it even better! I also added 1 TBS of lemon juice. Next time I'll add a little salt to the cooked mixture, use less sugar (1/2 or 3/4 C) and mash the cooked strawberries.

My Granny used to make a similar strawberry pie except she would take a shortcut and use Wick's Pies Strawberry Glaze. The pie filling in this recipe puts Wick's to shame and sets up very nicely. Thank you for sharing!
I think this recipe turns out great. I usually add my cornstarch to the sugar, instead of adding more water, and since I make strawberry jam, I add that if the filling seems to thin.
Didn't set. Too sweet.
